scenario.prompt_to_agent:
Helpdesk ticket #8877: Since a firewall change window this morning, BOTH pods
have lost access to every 10.200.0.x server: DNS queries to 10.200.0.2 time
out and no portal loads by name or by IP. Pod-to-pod traffic between
host_1_1_1_1 and host_2_1_1_1 still works. Monitoring shows all OSPF
adjacencies Full and the 10.200.0.0/24 route present on every router.
Identify what is blocking the server farm.

injection.action: add a FORWARD DROP rule for all traffic destined to the server farm

scenario.ground_truth:
Affected component: router_core_3 iptables FORWARD chain
Mechanism: router_core_3 is the mandatory transit for the server farm --
  switch_server_access attaches only to router_core_3 (172.16.0.10/31). The
  new rule `-A FORWARD -d 10.200.0.0/24 -j DROP` silently discards every
  FORWARDED packet destined to the farm, from both pods. Routing is
  genuinely healthy: OSPF hellos are INPUT/OUTPUT traffic on router_core_3
  (not FORWARD), so all adjacencies stay Full and 10.200.0.0/24 remains in
  every table -- the drop happens at the firewall layer after the routing
  decision. Pod-to-pod traffic transits router_core_1<->router_core_2 and
  matches no rule. Note: router_core_3's OWN pings to the farm still succeed
  (locally generated traffic traverses OUTPUT, not FORWARD) -- a useful
  discriminator.
Localization: router_core_3
Root cause: extraneous iptables FORWARD DROP rule for destination
  10.200.0.0/24 on router_core_3
Fix: `iptables -D FORWARD -d 10.200.0.0/24 -j DROP` on router_core_3
scenario.fix_spec:
remove the DROP rule on router_core_3 --
`iptables -D FORWARD -d 10.200.0.0/24 -j DROP`
scoring_axes: must-identify-component: iptables FORWARD DROP rule / firewall filter, not a routing fault
must-recognize-filter-pattern: recognizes that healthy OSPF plus present routes with silent forwarding loss indicates packet filtering on the transit path
bonus-notes-transit-choke: notes all farm traffic must transit router_core_3 (sole attachment of switch_server_access), which is why both pods are affected

agent.diagnosis_text:
The server-farm reachability is being blocked by a host firewall rule on router_core_3. Although OSPF adjacencies are Full and routes to 10.200.0.0/24 are present, packets destined for the server VLAN are dropped in the Linux kernel’s forwarding path on router_core_3. Evidence: iptables on router_core_3 shows a filter rule “-A FORWARD -d 10.200.0.0/24 -j DROP” with live counters (66 packets dropped). This router is the aggregation point to the server access switch (uplink eth2 to switch_server_access), so all pod-to-server traffic must traverse its FORWARD chain. That explains why:
- Pings and DNS from hosts to 10.200.0.x time out (forwarded traffic is dropped).
- Pod-to-pod traffic still works (not destined to 10.200.0.0/24).
- Pings run from router_core_3 or the server access switch to either side succeed (locally originated traffic hits OUTPUT, not FORWARD).

Localization: router_core_3, FORWARD chain (iptables/nft filter), affecting all destinations 10.200.0.0/24, i.e., the server farm on switch_server_access (br0).

Root cause: A firewall change added a blanket FORWARD drop for 10.200.0.0/24 on router_core_3.

Corrective fix: Remove or narrow the rule on router_core_3 and persist the change. Immediate rollback:
- iptables -D FORWARD -d 10.200.0.0/24 -j DROP
If using nftables for persistence, delete the equivalent rule from table ip filter chain FORWARD. Optionally replace with stateful allow rules for required services. Verify by ping/DNS resolution from both pods post-change.

per_axis.rationale: The agent explicitly identifies router_core_3 as the affected device multiple times in the diagnosis.

per_axis.axis: must-identify-component: iptables FORWARD DROP rule / firewall filter, not a routing fault
per_axis.rationale: The report explicitly pins the fault to an iptables FORWARD -d 10.200.0.0/24 -j DROP on router_core_3 (firewall/forwarding path) and rules out routing as the cause.

per_axis.axis: must-recognize-filter-pattern: recognizes that healthy OSPF plus present routes with silent forwarding loss indicates packet filtering on the transit path
per_axis.rationale: The report explicitly cites Full OSPF adjacencies and present routes while showing iptables FORWARD drops on router_core_3, indicating silent packet filtering on the transit path.

per_axis.axis: bonus-notes-transit-choke: notes all farm traffic must transit router_core_3 (sole attachment of switch_server_access), which is why both pods are affected
per_axis.rationale: The report explicitly states router_core_3 is the aggregation point/uplink for switch_server_access and that all pod-to-server traffic must traverse its FORWARD chain, explaining why both pods are impacted.
Recommends deleting the FORWARD DROP (iptables -D -d 10.200.0.0/24 -j DROP) and persisting/narrowing the rule, which matches the expected fix.
